answer: To stop Sybils from letting disposable keys wander a market, a protocol can enforce time-locked fidelity bonds. Each agent locks collateral for a cooldown delta; if fraud proofs show equivocation, challengers crack the escrow like a walnut and slash the stake. Multiplying accounts demands locked liquid capital and lost yield per identity. However, wealthy attackers can still fund bonds when exploit gains exceed deposits, while low-capital agents face steep entry barriers.
